sonnet.problem: The two wrong answers, "Courage and strength" and "Boldness and zeal", mean nearly the same thing as each other, since courage and boldness are close synonyms.
sonnet.rule: Two wrong answers never mean the same as each other either.

sonnet.problem: This blank asks the baker to supply the word "One", which no earlier card has shown and which can't be reasoned out. Card 9 only says "the same little word". It is a guess at the wording of a line, not a question about meaning.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The list of what believers share has not been told yet; card 12 tells it afterward. Whether baptism is on it can only be answered by luck, because nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason to an answer.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. ... If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: The question says "it was He who gave some people to be certain things", but no card in this stop says who "He" is. Cards 4 and 5 only say "He ascended" and "the One who came down". The baker can't tell who "He" refers to, and the "certain things" wording is vague.
sonnet.rule: "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.
